task_specification.objective: Advance release convergence with two bounded surfaces: restore readable authored-cemetery composition and spatial integrity while preserving the intact map, and harden the dense-wave cost/qualification path so native hardware recapture can prove the 60 FPS contract without altering survivor-like combat causality.

diagnosis.root_cause: The authored cemetery package is intact but its release lighting/exposure crushes shadow detail and weakens landmark/perimeter readability. Dense-wave performance evidence is still rejected because all prior cycles ran on llvmpipe software rendering, so candidate-side bounded-cost work and an honest native-renderer recapture path are required without treating software numbers as qualification.

stop_conditions: Keep the native authored cemetery as one intact authoritative environment package; do not replace, duplicate, extract, or surgically edit imported world assets.
Do not relabel software-renderer evidence as hardware qualification or tune acceptance to the rejected llvmpipe measurements.
Do not expand into unrelated weapons, boss, lifecycle, or product-shell changes beyond the explicitly required choice-hierarchy behavior and dense-wave cost controls.
Stop when candidate-side repairs and deterministic receipts are ready for GameLoop Runtime/Tester recapture; host verdicts and issue closure remain outside Developer scope.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause strategy from prior evidence-only retries and transform tuning: rebalance world exposure/fill and verify native spatial bindings for visual readability, while tightening bounded dense-wave lifecycle/update budgets and renderer-gated receipts so hardware qualification can be recaptured truthfully.

code: Run Godot parse/import/static checks on every touched scene, script, and resource; verify no fatal load errors or invalid node paths.
Confirm the authored map remains a single intact runtime instance and no proxy floor, generated road patch, facade slice, backdrop, or duplicate landmark was introduced.

Exercise upgrade-draft data normalization and focus wiring with available keyboard, mouse, and gamepad paths; verify current values never use NEW/LOCKED placeholders and at most three changed rows render.
runtime: GameLoop Runtime/Tester must recapture release_convergence_authored_cemetery_composition_contract using shipped-camera baseline, spawn, critical-route, central-landmark, cardinal/perimeter, and near-contact/departure movement replay views; verify expand/larger traversable scale, external world/depth, collision alignment, boundary/perimeter containment, and no disappearance/occlusion drift.

GameLoop Runtime/Tester must recapture release_convergence_dense_performance_contract on the designated native hardware renderer at 1920x1080 for three complete prepare/advance/reset cycles, recording p50/p95/p99/worst frame times, retry deltas, renderer classification, and active resource counts.
Preserve and rerun host_godot_boot and native_godot_project checks; inspect runtime logs for recurring errors, freed-instance access, duplicate terminal transitions, or stuck pause state.
visual: Compare same-framing retest captures to the prior underexposed views: shadow detail, readable silhouettes, warm/cool hierarchy, central landmark, perimeter/external depth, and escape lanes must remain visible without flattening the night mood.
Inspect dense gameplay at representative visual density for clear enemy silhouettes, telegraphs, player separation, restrained effects, and no visible placeholders or matte/debug surfaces.

Inspect the choice draft at native viewport and supported UI scales for icon-led hierarchy, truthful compact deltas, restrained copy, stable card dimensions, and distinct keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states.

done_when: The intact authored cemetery is visibly readable from the shipped gameplay camera and HUD-free spawn, critical-route, and landmark/perimeter views: warm player/landmark accents, moonlit cool shadows, graves, paths, external depth, and the central building or other landmark remain discernible without crushed blacks.

The arena has expand or larger traversable scale beyond a camera-sized pad, with a coherent external world or external depth beyond the playable boundary; ordinary movement or movement replay along the critical route and full perimeter keeps the player and representative enemies visible.

Visible landmark footprints and their collision agree: no pass-through, disappearance, or camera-occlusion drift when approaching, contacting, and departing the central building/landmark or perimeter boundary.

Upgrade/weapon choice presentation remains an authored visual hierarchy: a recognizable silhouette/icon leads each option, compact stat icons show truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant deltas, unchanged/exhaustive rows are omitted, and NEW or LOCKED never appears as a placeholder in the CURRENT value column.
Choice cards retain restrained copy and distinct keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus/hover/selected/unavailable states with debounced confirmation and stable dimensions.
tasks.instructions: Repair the presentation around the existing cemetery instance rather than replacing its authored package. Rebalance WorldEnvironment, directional/fill lighting, fog, and landmark lights to lift shadow detail while preserving the warm-versus-cool nighttime hierarchy and native streets, graves, trees, fences, mausoleum, keeper post, and cracked bell. Check the product-owned spatial contract, collision anchors, camera framing/occlusion handling, and playable boundary so the larger traversable scale and external world remain coherent under ordinary movement. In the same bounded presentation pass, preserve or repair the existing upgrade-draft renderer so silhouettes/icons dominate, current-to-new values are truthful and limited to decision-relevant deltas, and all keyboard/mouse/gamepad focus states are visible; do not turn cards into text tables.
tasks.title: Expose the cemetery and keep choices legible

done_when: The candidate keeps the dense-wave contract renderer-gated: software/llvmpipe runs remain explicitly rejected and cannot count as native qualification, while a deterministic hardware-eligibility receipt and complete three-cycle recapture entrypoint are available.

The dominant product-owned dense cost is bounded through lifecycle pooling/reset, staggered steering/target queries, presentation refresh cadence, effect/light/voice caps, or equivalent controls; no unbounded live nodes, callbacks, memory, or duplicated audio appear across repeated Retry cycles.

On the representative 25–40 enemy profile, automatic attacks, enemy motion, damage/death/drop causality, readable telegraphs, and Bellkeeper phase behavior remain intact while dense presentation work is throttled or capped.

Runtime telemetry exposes frame-time distribution plus active enemies/projectiles/pickups/effects/lights/audio voices and reset deltas needed for host-side native-renderer qualification, without claiming closure from software measurements.
tasks.instructions: Treat the prior llvmpipe result as rejected evidence, not a tuning target. Harden the existing dense-wave profile and responsible runtime systems with a bounded-cost strategy: inspect and, where needed, reduce per-frame neighbor/target queries, animation/presentation updates, dynamic lights, particles/effects, and high-churn allocations using deterministic buckets, caches, pooling, and reset-safe caps. Keep ordinary wave escalation, automatic combat causality, legal targeting, telegraph visibility, boss phases, and run restart semantics unchanged. Emit explicit renderer classification/hardware eligibility and requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts so GameLoop Runtime/Tester can repeat the same three native-hardware cycles; do not relabel software output or promise host-side qualification.
